sample_unit: FAQs on male infertility submitted to each of five LLMs under two prompting conditions

links.outcome: Readability (FRE, SMOG) of LLM responses to male infertility FAQs without context
links.effect: Unprompted, DeepSeek was most readable (FRE 46.28±6.86; SMOG 11.71±0.76); Claude least readable (FRE 23.83±12.29; SMOG 16.37±2.47), i.e., difficult, college-level text.
links.quote: In the non-prompted condition, DeepSeek generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 46.28±6.86; mean SMOG 11.71±0.76), whereas Claude produced the least readable outputs (mean FRE 23.83±12.29; mean SMOG 16.37±2.47).

links.outcome: Change in readability with contextual lay-patient prompting versus no context
links.effect: Readability improved across all models after prompting; Grok best (FRE 69.71±6.09; SMOG 9.96±1.04).
links.quote: After prompting, Grok generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 69.71±6.09; mean SMOG 9.96±1.04), and readability improved across all models.

unlisted_practices: Contextual prompting instructing the LLM to explain to a lay patient to improve readability

screen.practice: contextual prompting for lay reading level
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of a prompt engineering safeguard (prompting for lay audience comprehension/reading level) compared to standard prompting on the readability of LLM responses to patient FAQs.

primary.practice: contextual prompting for lay audience readability
